title: Somalia's Constitutional Countdown: 11 Days to May 15 — May 10 Talks Face Long Odds as Piracy, Al-Shabaab Crisis Compound
detail: As of May 4, 2026, Somalia faces the simultaneous convergence of three interconnected crises at their most acute phase. The constitutional crisis enters its final 11 days: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term expires May 15, the last parliament sat more than three weeks ago (mandate expired April 14), and both Puntland and Jubbaland have declared the current legal framework illegitimate. Mohamud's invitation to the Somali Future Council for May 10 talks — issued May 1 and welcomed by the UN, EU, and UK — represents the last realistic diplomatic window, but the structural distance between the parties remains vast: the opposition rejects the March 2026 constitutional amendments (disputed quorum), and the FGS has shown no sign of withdrawing or renegotiating them. Simultaneously, Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal in Hiiraan Region (Day 15 since the April 19 seizure, with the SNA counter-offensive stalled), demonstrating the real-world security cost of governance paralysis. At sea, the piracy crisis has reached 'severe' threat level: the Honour 25 tanker (17 crew, Day 9 of captivity), the Sward cargo vessel (15 crew), and now the MT Eureka (12 crew, hijacked May 2) are all under pirate control off the Puntland coast, while EU NAVFOR attributes the surge to the Iran War diverting naval resources. The International Crisis Group has warned that failure to reach a deal on May 10 risks triggering the most severe constitutional breakdown in Somalia's post-2012 federal order — with opposition groups formally declaring a dual-authority scenario and potentially establishing parallel institutions. Somalia's humanitarian situation remains catastrophic: 6.5 million food insecure, 1.85 million children at acute malnutrition risk, and the $852M response plan only 13.4% funded.

media.caption: ICG: Somalia faces constitutional breakdown if May 10 talks fail — 11 days to President Mohamud's May 15 term expiry with no electoral roadmap agreed
